Do you ever feel like you're playing a part that isn't really you? That's the "Role-Self" (the personality we built to please and manage the people around us), and as we grow up it gets locked in by Dopamine and DeltaFosB, so often your addiction is just what keeps it running. That's why I built this protocol to go after the chemistry holding the false persona in place, so the person you were before the trauma (your "True-Self") can come back out.

So with Neurological De-Armoring, I'm fixing the underpinnings first, instead of redecorating. The way it works is that Ketones (BHB) block HDAC, an enzyme that keeps genes switched off, and together with Glutamate modulation that makes the protocol a kind of metabolic solvent, softening the "concrete" in the brainstem. That's what lets us dig under the house and pour a new foundation, and only then update the psychological software upstairs.

The Anti-Breakthrough (Micro-Dosing): Have long therapy sessions ever left you wrecked for days? That's because, as Dr. Perry found, the "therapeutic window" for a dysregulated brain is often only seconds long, and a sensitized, armored nervous system just can't take in sixty minutes of trauma processing. So for now, the "hour-long breakthrough" has to wait.

Instead, the goal is Micro-Dosing Safety: 30 seconds of regulated breathing, twenty times a day. Think of it more as physical therapy for a broken nervous system than as running a marathon, where how often you do it matters more than how hard you push.

The Signal Dial (GluD Receptors): NMDA isn't the only control, though. Johns Hopkins researchers have recently discovered that the brain also uses GluD receptors as a kind of master volume knob, so if NMDA is the spark, GluD sets the baseline "hum" of the synapse. And in an armored state, that dial often gets jammed, either on "High" (Cerebellar Ataxia/Hyper-vigilance) or on "Low" (Apathy/Schizotypy).

The Repair (Leucine/L-Serine): L-Serine is what the brain makes D-Serine from, so it can help recalibrate the GluD "Volume Dial" and make therapy sessions that end with low fear and a sense of mastery stick better. The catch is that the conversion is inefficient, which is why some people take D-serine itself instead (higher risk, but also higher benefit). And Leucine is there for structural repair, while it also tunes synaptic gain, which is what eases the "itchy brain" feeling.

The Governor (Agmatine): Is your Glutamate Storm the hot, itchy, reactive, pain-y, rumination-heavy kind? Then agmatine is the optional "voltage governor" I'd look at. That's because it may help when the problem isn't just excess glutamate in the synapse but NMDA/GluN2B over-reactivity, so think of it as a brake for that state, something to use while you're in it rather than a daily foundation nutrient.

Important conflict: don't take agmatine in the same session as D-Serine/DCS-style exposure or EMDR work. The reason is that agmatine partly brakes NMDA activity, and NMDA-dependent learning and memory updating is exactly what those tools are there to support. So use agmatine for storm control, but not right before a session where the goal is deliberate reconsolidation.
